solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Strengthen control on behalf of Church of England

parts.note: a rein is what controls a horse, so control means rein
acting for someone is acting on their behalf

explanation.surface: A call to bolster authority on behalf of the established Church.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster something is to make it stronger, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Withdraws religious education pamphlets

parts.note: RE is the school subject religious education
tracts are short pamphlets, often religious

explanation.surface: A school pulls its religious leaflets.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to take back a statement, a verb synonym for withdraw.

clue.text: Fair enough concealing intense anger

indicators.note: the phrase conceals the letters within it, across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone agreeing 'fair enough' while hiding their fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for wrath, a synonym of strong anger.

clue.text: Learner in market displaying natural talent

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: a fair is a market or show
L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: A novice at a market shows a born gift for selling.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is an instinctive aptitude, a synonym for a natural gift.

clue.text: Banner, excellent example

parts.note: royal can mean splendid or excellent, as in a royal welcome
a standard is a model or exemplar to follow

explanation.surface: A flag held up as a fine example.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Standard is the flag flown to show the British monarch is present.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Standard is the sovereign's flag, so an example of a banner.

clue.text: As one man sees changes

indicators.note: a word that changes is altered in form, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A single man sees things alter.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means all together as a group, the same idea as acting together.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed about diamonds

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in business letters
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone blushing over a matter involving diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is embarrassed flushes in the face, turning that colour.

clue.text: Ice, mostly, round Irish lake

indicators.note: mostly means the word for ice without its last letter

parts.note: ice can mean cool reserve or aloofness of manner
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Ice largely surrounding a lake in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice' suggests frozen water, but it means cool reserve of manner; 'mostly' trims RESERVE to RESERV.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a large artificial body of stored water, so a kind of lake.

clue.text: Accomplished poet, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means said out loud, a sound-alike signal

parts.note: John Donne was the English metaphysical poet

explanation.surface: A poet described as gifted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accomplished has been completed or finished, so it is achieved.

clue.text: Male brought in injured party for treatment

indicators.note: something brought in is placed within the other letters
an injured thing is damaged and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man is admitted after a party leaves him hurt, needing medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' scrambles the party word to TRAPY, and 'brought in' places the male pronoun just after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is a course of remedial care, a synonym for medical treatment.

clue.text: Male, when working, is one who dresses stone

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A working man is a stoneworker.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason shapes and finishes building stone; dressing stone is his trade.

clue.text: Flower festival failing to open

indicators.note: a word failing to open loses its first letter

parts.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival

explanation.surface: A bloom at a festival which does not open.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like garden plant, an example of a bloom.

clue.text: Song from old musical, tap-danced originally with special footwear

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of tap-danced
special here means specially arranged, so the letters are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A number from a vintage show, tap-danced in particular shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' scrambles the shoe word to EAFORTWO, placed after the opening letter of tap-danced.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known number from the 1925 musical No, No, Nanette, an example of a show song.

clue.text: Polish in Ulster, working

indicators.note: letters set working are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone from Poland employed in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality, but it is the noun meaning shine. Ulster is the northern province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is the sheen on a surface, which is what a polish gives.

clue.text: Small mountain most difficult to endure

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
Everest is the world's highest mountain

explanation.surface: A little mountain proves the hardest one to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Severest is the superlative of severe, meaning harshest, so it is the hardest to bear.

clue.text: Sausage dish: one hotel had it prepared

indicators.note: food that is prepared is made up from ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A hotel serves up a sausage meal one guest had made for them.
explanation.walkthrough: Toad-in-the-hole is a British dish of sausages baked in Yorkshire pudding batter.
explanation.definitionFit: This British dish is sausages baked in batter, an example of a sausage meal.

clue.text: Current admirer cheers the king of Spain's eldest daughter?

definitions.text: the king of Spain's eldest daughter?

parts.note: in means current or fashionable
a fan is an admirer
ta and cheers are both informal British thanks

explanation.surface: A modern fan thanks the Spanish princess.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: an infanta is any daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese king.
explanation.definitionFit: Infanta is the title of a daughter of the Spanish monarch, so the eldest is one example.

clue.text: Black box caught out research scientist

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: the letter for caught is taken out of the word for box

parts.note: a coffin is the box a body is buried in
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A black box recorder found, leaving a scientist in the lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes C from COFFIN to leave OFFIN. Boffin is British slang for a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is informal British slang for a scientist doing research work, especially technical.

clue.text: Swear nothing's missing from racetrack

indicators.note: a letter missing from a word has been taken out of it

parts.note: a racecourse is a racetrack
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A punter swears at an empty racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to use bad language, a verb synonym for swearing.

clue.text: Comfort food and drink

definitions.meaning: to comfort is to encourage or gladden someone
good ... is festive fare to eat and drink

explanation.surface: Consolation through something to eat and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to hearten someone; the old noun sense is fare served at a feast.

clue.text: Unknown individual in band

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown, like x and y
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A mystery person in a music group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a music group, but it means a strip or belt of area.
explanation.definitionFit: A band in this sense is a stretch or belt of territory, which is an area.

clue.text: Frequently fall in value? Not shares, initially

indicators.note: not this letter means the letter is removed

parts.note: prices soften when they ease or fall

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word shares

explanation.surface: A question about whether share prices often drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Often and frequently are adverb synonyms meaning many times.

clue.text: Typical woman admitting age? Just the opposite!

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside another
this reverses the stated arrangement, so it is the age word that lets in the woman

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A typical woman owning up to her age, or rather not.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly the woman would hold AGE; 'Just the opposite!' flips it so AGE holds VERA: A-VERA-GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Average describes what is normal or ordinary, so it fits typical as an adjective.

clue.text: Has broken wood

indicators.note: something broken is shattered, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has snapped a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a hard pale timber from the tree of that name, an example of wood.

clue.text: Conceit, for example, shown by Oscar

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Vanity, as displayed by an Oscar winner.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar suggests a vain film star, but it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceit is excessive self-regard, an inflated sense of self, which is the ego.

clue.text: Trees attracting much interest in Hampshire town

parts.note: alders are trees of the birch family
a hot topic attracts much interest

explanation.surface: Trees in an English county town drawing a lot of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldershot is a town in Hampshire, an English county, known as a British Army base.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldershot is a garrison town in Hampshire, southern England, so an example of one.
